text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Building at Har Homan begins, Netanyahu considers additional 1,000 homes for Palestinians
- Justice Minister Tsachi Hanegbi questioned again by police over suspected corruption in appointment of attorney-general Roni Bar-On
- Internal Security Minister Kahalani: We're ready for any flareup
- U.S. concerned over violence
- Jordan island wasn't on itinerary of outing that ended in girls massacre by soldier, school principle testifies
HAARETZ
- Warnings of terrorist attacks in Israel and the territories
- Prosecution sources: Justice Minister Hanegbi should suspend himself because of police investigation
- Ex-air force chief Bodinger often responded "I don't remember" to inquiry panel over cable accident
- International bank director-general monthly wage is 370,000 shekels
- Arafat calls to refrain from violence; rules out meeting Netanyahu for the sake of meeting
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Labour leader Shimon Peres persuading knesset members to join unity government with Netanyahu
- Arafat: no to violence. Netanyahu: he approved attacks
MAARIV
- Netanyahu: there is no better timing for building
- Poll: most of public favours Har Homa, but not now
GLOBES
- Africa-Israel to reexamine policy of closing mall on Saturday
- International bank profits for 1996 grow by 10.2 pct
- Directors of insurance companies to reject demand they resign over cartel rulings
